newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACIL oil royalty trust tips 10 pct return.
newsitem.headline: ACIL oil royalty trust tips 10 pct return.

text.p: Australia Consolidated Investments Ltd (ACIL) said on Monday its Bass Strait oil and gas royalty float, Bass Strait Oil Trust, forecasts an average 10.5 percent yield for unitholders paying the top marginal tax rate.
The offer cashes in most of ACIL's share of a royalty over Australia's largest oil and gas production area, Bass Strait.
ACIL is 98 percent owned by New Zealand investment group, Brierley Investments Ltd.

"Investment returns on the units will be linked directly to revenues from Bass Strait which in 1996 accounted for 37 percent of Australia's oil production," Paul Collins, chairman of the trust's manager, told a media briefing.
The Bass Strait Royalty is a 2.5 percent overriding royalty relating to all oil and gas produced by the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd from parts of the Bass Strait field.
The trust will hold a part of the royalty called the Weeks Royalty, which receives 55.11 percent of payments currently made by Esso and BHP under the terms of the royalty.
Bass Strait Oil Trust will offer 44 million units at A$5.00 per unit to Australian investors to raise A$220 million.

The units will be redeemed progressively over their 10 year life through 20 equal half-yearly payments of 25 cents each. ACIL has guranteed the payments which will be secured by a letter of credit from National Australia Bank Ltd.

Collins said the trust had received a private tax ruling from the Australian government which meant that the capital redemption payments would reduce the cost base of the units for capital gains tax purposes.

"The trust takes the total Weeks royalty revenue for the next ten years, repackages it so it (the revenue) is tax enhanced for investors, and sends it back out to investors without reduction," Collins said.

Brierley director Don Conway told reporters the company had spent five years resolving a number of issues surrounding the Weeks Royalty after gaining the interest through its takeover of ACIL in 1992.
Conway said ACIL would retain the residual interest in the Weeks Royalty which he said had been valued at A$174 million.
ACIL said the minimum investment in the trust would be A$5,000 with the offer opening on May 26, closing on June 20 and units expected to debut on the Australian Stock Exchange in early July.
